acceptance_criteria.criterion: cloneRepository() emits console.warn for any URL starting with 'http://'.
cloneRepository() emits console.warn for any URL starting with 'git://'.
cloneRepository() does NOT emit console.warn for 'https://' or 'ssh://' URLs.
The warning message contains the word 'cleartext' and the offending protocol.
The URL is not rejected — the clone proceeds (or fails for unrelated reasons) normally.
Test: a console.warn spy confirms the warning is emitted when an http:// URL is supplied.
All pre-existing tests in git-clone.test.ts continue to pass.

summary: Added cleartext URL warning to cloneRepository() in git-clone.ts: emits console.warn immediately after the isAllowedUrl() guard when the URL starts with 'http://' or 'git://'.
Warning message format: 'Warning: cloning over cleartext protocol (http://). Consider using https:// or ssh:// for security.'
Added 3 new tests to git-clone.test.ts: (1) warns for http:// URLs, (2) warns for git:// URLs, (3) does NOT warn for https:// or ssh:// URLs.

comments.note: The test spy uses direct assignment (console.warn = ...) rather than a framework spy API (e.g. vi.spyOn). This is appropriate for the project's node:test runner which lacks a built-in spy API, and restoring in a finally block is safe. No change needed.

The cleartext-warning block in git-clone.ts uses a simple startsWith check rather than URL.protocol parsing. This is consistent with the existing isAllowedUrl() pattern (also uses startsWith) and avoids a URL constructor call that could throw on malformed URLs reaching this branch.
No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent.

summary: Full Verification Stack executed: build check, AC verification, regression testing, and edge-case stress testing.
Build: `npm test` compiles TypeScript and runs all tests via `tsc && node --test dist/tests/*.test.js`. Build and runtime check passed with 0 errors.

AC Verification: All 7 acceptance criteria independently verified by running `node --test dist/tests/git-clone.test.js` with SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1. All 15 tests pass (1 network test skipped as designed).
The 3 new cleartext tests all pass: http:// warns, git:// warns, https:// and ssh:// do not warn.
Regression: Full suite of 340 tests (341 total, 1 skipped) passes with 0 failures — no regressions introduced.

Edge cases reviewed: case-sensitive startsWith consistent with isAllowedUrl() pattern; bare http:// URL (no host) correctly warns then delegates failure to git; console.warn restoration in finally block is safe against exceptions; warning fires before runGit() invocation (lines 60-65 vs 83).

comments.note: Edge case: HTTP:// (uppercase) would bypass the startsWith check and not emit a warning. This is consistent with isAllowedUrl() behavior (also case-sensitive startsWith) and git itself normalises schemes, so in practice only lowercase protocol strings reach this code. Not a bug.
No observations — code is clean and consistent. Implementation is minimal and correctly scoped.

summary: Reviewed 2 modified files (src/git/git-clone.ts, src/tests/git-clone.test.ts). No new dependencies introduced. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. Security sign-off: PASS. The change proactively improves security posture by warning on cleartext transports (A02). Injection vectors remain closed (spawn with shell:false, allowlist guard upstream of new code). One Low/Info observation recorded regarding case-sensitivity of the startsWith check, consistent with existing codebase patterns and not exploitable.

comments.note: A02 — Cryptographic Failures: The new cleartext-warning block (git-clone.ts:60-65) affirmatively improves the security posture by alerting callers that http:// and git:// are unencrypted transports. Warning fires after the isAllowedUrl() allowlist guard and before runGit() invocation, so no bypass is possible. No remediation needed — this is a positive control.

A03 — Injection: runGit() (git-cli.ts) spawns with shell:false and passes all arguments as a pre-split string array. The URL and destination are array elements, not concatenated into a shell string. No shell-injection vector introduced or present in the modified code.

A02 / Defence-in-depth: The cleartext warning uses case-sensitive startsWith('http://') and startsWith('git://'). An uppercase scheme such as HTTP:// would bypass the warning. This mirrors the existing isAllowedUrl() pattern (also case-sensitive) and is not exploitable in practice — git normalises protocol schemes before URLs typically reach application code. Recommend documenting this assumption, but no blocking remediation required.
No further security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed against the modified files. No Critical or High issues identified.

summary: Code review PASS. Implementation is minimal, correctly scoped, and architecturally consistent. The cleartext-warning block (git-clone.ts:60–65) sits in exactly the right place — after the allowlist guard and before runGit() invocation — so there is no bypass path and no behaviour change for safe protocols. The protocol derivation (re-evaluating startsWith rather than slicing the URL) is slightly redundant but harmless and already noted by the Developer. All three new tests are well-structured, use safe finally-block spy restoration, and assert both positive and negative cases. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: git-clone.ts:61 — the protocol string is derived by a second pair of startsWith checks rather than slicing url directly (e.g. url.slice(0, url.indexOf('://')+3)). The current approach is clear and completely correct; the slight redundancy is a Fix-Forward candidate but not worth a bounce. Leaving as-is — readability wins here.

No further architectural observations — code is clean and consistent with the surrounding codebase. Implementation, QA, and Security pipelines all PASS with zero high-priority findings.
